thread:
Maria L.: Hey team — AcmeHealth POC is getting intermittent 500s during an embeddings bulk run. Demo paused. Saw spike ~16:03 UTC, errors say \"server_error: capacity_throttle\" and lots of \"queue full\" in the runtime logs. Anyone available to triage?

Aj Patel: On it. Can you paste a sample request_id and the deployment name? Also what model variant + region?

Maria L.: request_id=cli_20270318_160315_az1, deployment=acme-poc-emb-v2, model=redwood-embed-2.0-q4, region=us-west-2

Maria L.: quick curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-2.0-q4","input":["...lots of docs..."],"batch_size":64}'
```

Kyle (SRE): I see the runtime traces for that request_id. Errors originate from worker queue overflow while autoscaler was still spinning up new nodes. Scaling took ~48s to add GPUs. Backpressure hit at ~15s and returned 500s.

Samir - Sales Eng: Customer is running a single-shot large batch as part of demo — they ramped concurrency and batch together which probably pushed peak. Any short-term mitigations we can ask them to try?

Aj Patel: Short-term: reduce batch_size to 16-32, limit client concurrency to 4, add retries with exponential backoff. Also enable prefix KV cache if embedding inputs share prefixes. That usually cuts token work.

Kyle (SRE): Agreed. Also recommend enabling fallback to the CPU-friendly variant for non-latency-critical parts: set \"prefer_model\" to \"redwood-embed-2.0-fallback\" in the request policy so requests hit fallback if GPU capacity delayed. It avoids 5xx while preserving throughput.

Maria L.: Can you show the exact header/param we should give the customer?

Aj Patel: Example policy: 
```
{
  \"routing\": {\"prefer_model\": \"redwood-embed-2.0-fallback\", \"max_concurrency\": 4},
  \"client_hints\": {\"batch_size\": 32}
}
```
Send as \"X-Redwood-Routing\" JSON string or via SDK options.

Maria L.: copy. I'll push that to them now. Any server-side config changes we can do so this doesn't recur for PoC traffic?

Kyle (SRE): We can tighten autoscale trigger to start earlier for that customer's org (lower CPU/KV queue threshold) or pre-warm 1 extra node during demo windows. But that requires infra approval.

Elaine (AE): Customer is demoing at 16:45 UTC today. Can we do a temporary pre-warm? They'll likely sign if demo goes well.

Kyle (SRE): I'll approve a 30m pre-warm for acme-poc-emb-v2 (adding 2 GPUs) if we coordinate with infra ops. That should remove scaling lag.

infra-bot: Autoscaler event: triggered scale-up for acme-poc-emb-v2 (+2 nodes). Estimated finish ~1769810100. :gear:

Aj Patel: For debugging gather: redwood logs --deployment acme-poc-emb-v2 --since 20m and share the last 200 lines. Also include CPU/GPU utilization and queue_depth metric charts.

Maria L.: Pasted logs to thread gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/acme-poc-logs-17698 (contains the queue_full traces and worker stack).

Samir - Sales Eng: Nice. Also offering them a quick patch: ask them to run this load script that throttles batch into chunks:
```
# python example
for chunk in chunked(inputs, 32):
  client.embeddings.create(model='redwood-embed-2.0-q4', input=chunk)
```
This reduces simultaneous token work.

Maria L.: We applied the fallback header + limited concurrency and the demo resumed, errors dropped to zero. Customer will re-run full batch after pre-warm.

Kyle (SRE): Follow-up: we'll look at autoscale thresholds — proposal: reduce queue_depth threshold from 80% to 60% for POC-sized pools and add a short-lived burst_pool that can absorb first 30s of ramp. I'll open infra ticket.

Aj Patel: Ticket created: INF-2026-732 (attach logs + repro). Assigning to infra on-call.

Elaine (AE): Thanks team — I'll tell AcmeHealth we've got a pre-warm window and a mitigation in place.

Maria L.: Thanks everyone. I'll confirm after their second run. :thumbsup:
